newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: No technical fault found in Gulf Air accident.
newsitem.headline: No technical fault found in Gulf Air accident.

text.p: Initial investigation has not found any technical fault in the Gulf Air Airbus plane that aborted takeoff this month at Abu Dhabi airport, a civil aviation official said on Thursday.

Mohammad Ghanem al-Gaith, director general of the Abu Dhabi civil aviation authority, said initial analysis of the black box carried out in France did not find "any technical problem with the plane that made it veer off (the runway)."
In comments carried by the official UAE news agency WAM, he said the investigation was continuing into the incident on March 10 when the British pilot aborted takeoff.
The plane, which lost its front wheel and skidded along the runway on its nose, was on a flight from Bahrain to Cairo. The pilot and several passengers were injured.
Bahrain-based Gulf Air is jointly owned by the governments of Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar.
